finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: user-supplied URL passed to file_get_contents, which fetches http/https/ftp URLs server-side. Response size is returned (length oracle).

trace.note: Branch taken on POST with 'feed' parameter present; no auth check on this branch
Attacker-controlled value passed directly to file_get_contents
Returns strlen of fetched body, a length-only oracle for internal probing

finding.guards_checked: No session/admin check on this branch; no scheme allowlist; no host/IP denylist (loopback, RFC1918, link-local 169.254.169.254); no port restriction; no redirect control. file:// also reachable (related local file read).

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']); there is no require_admin() or other auth call on this branch (require_admin is only called at import.php:18, inside the set_webhook branch). Nothing between line 11 and the sink at line 12 validates the scheme, host, IP, or port.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: import.php:11 branches on attacker-supplied POST 'feed' with no session check, import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] directly to file_get_contents, and import.php:13 echoes strlen($xml), so an unauthenticated remote attacker controls the URL and gets a response-length oracle. The one caveat is that http/ftp fetching through file_get_contents depends on allow_url_fopen, which is a php.ini setting not present in this directory; PHP's default is On, so this does not refute the finding.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: user-supplied URL passed to curl_init and executed with curl_exec; response discarded, handler echoes 'ok'.

trace.note: Branch taken when set_webhook POST parameter is present
Value assigned to $hook with no transformation
curl_exec performs the server-side request; body not returned

finding.guards_checked: Session admin check only (authorization, not URL validation). No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS/REDIR_PROTOCOLS, no CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION restriction, no host/IP allowlist. Whether is_admin can be set by unprivileged users is outside this directory and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is an authorization check only; there is no URL validation, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS or CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS, no host allowlist, and no CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION restriction anywhere in the directory. The only CURLOPT_ in the directory is CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER at import.php:21.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: import.php:17-22 does what the candidate says, and the response is discarded with only "ok" echoed at line 23. The source is gated by $_SESSION['is_admin'] at import.php:5, and nothing in this directory ever sets that key, so whether a low-privilege attacker can reach this sink depends on code outside the directory that was not checked, which the candidate also says. If is_admin can only be set by administrators, the finding is not an attacker-controllable SSRF and should be downgraded or refuted. Separately, import.php:11-14 is an unauthenticated file_get_contents($_POST['feed']) sink that is a distinct and more exposed candidate.
